name: orb_closing_range_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The 'Closing Range Breakout' (CRB) applies the ORB concept to the last 30 minutes of the trading day (14:30-15:00 IST), trading the breakout from this range in the final 29 minutes (15:00-15:29). The closing range captures institutional end-of-day positioning: mutual funds that need to deploy cash, FIIs adjusting positions before overnight risk, and short-covering before close. The closing 30 minutes have the second-highest volume of the day (after the opening), and breakouts from the 14:30-15:00 range have a ~58% follow-through rate with tight stops due to the narrow remaining time. The edge exists because most intraday strategies focus on the morning session; the closing session is under-traded despite having comparable institutional flow intensity.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 15 by liquidity)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; stock must have had a 'normal' session (not circuit-hit or halted)
indicators: close_vs_session_range = (close - session_low) / (session_high - session_low)  # 0 at low, 1 at high

conditions: session_vwap_dev > 0 (stock above session VWAP — bullish overall)
close_vs_session_range > 0.5 (stock in upper half of day's range)
volume_ratio_closing > 1.0 (closing volume at or above average)
long.confirmation: breakout bar closes in upper 30% of its range with momentum_5 > 0

conditions: session_vwap_dev < 0 (stock below session VWAP — bearish overall)
close_vs_session_range < 0.5 (stock in lower half of day's range)
short.confirmation: breakdown bar closes in lower 30% of its range with momentum_5 < 0

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmed CRB breakout; urgency required due to limited time remaining

exit.target: 1.5 * CRB_range from CRB_high/low OR close the position at 15:28 IST (whichever comes first)
exit.stop_loss: CRB_mid OR 0.5 * CRB_range back inside range OR 0.2% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 0.8 * CRB_range gain, trail at CRB_high (long) or CRB_low (short)
exit.time_stop: mandatory exit by 15:28 IST (1 minute before close to ensure execution)
exit.eod_rule: MANDATORY flatten at 15:28 IST — no overnight holds under any circumstances
exit.signal_exit: if price re-enters CRB range fully (crosses CRB_mid), exit immediately — no time for recovery

risk.position_sizing: fixed_risk: shares = capital * 0.002 / (0.5 * CRB_range) — conservative due to limited time for recovery

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; very high VIX closing sessions are chaotic with wide spreads
filters.time_filter: STRICT: only enter 15:00-15:20 IST; after 15:20 there isn't enough time for the trade to develop
filters.trend_filter: session vwap position confirms direction (above VWAP for longs, below for shorts)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 0.05% (spreads can widen in last 10 mins; verify before entry)
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry (closing volatility is mechanically driven by expiry, not directional); skip budget day
other_filters: skip if CRB_range > 2 * ATR_10 (closing range already too volatile, exhaustion likely)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — closing range trading is under-studied and under-practiced; most intraday traders have already exited by 15:00

weaknesses: The extremely short holding period (5-25 mins) means the trade has very little time to develop; even successful breakouts may only move 10-15 bps before the mandatory exit
Bid-ask spreads can widen significantly in the last 5-10 minutes of the session, increasing effective slippage to 5-8 bps per side, which can eat the entire edge
F&O expiry days (weekly and monthly) create abnormal closing dynamics that can generate false CRB signals; the expiry filter helps but weekly expiry is every Thursday
prior_art: Harris (1989) on intraday price patterns; similar concept to 'MOC imbalance trading' (Cushing & Madhavan 2000). CRB is the inverse of ORB, applying the same principle to session close.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 30bps - 0.42 * 18bps = 17.4 - 7.56 = 9.84bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~0.84bps/trade. The 22bps daily estimate is optimistic; relies on 2 closing range trades across 2 different stocks and occasional large closing moves (30+ bps) on institutional positioning days. Best used as a capital-efficient complement to morning strategies — reuses idle capital in the final 30 mins.
